rows.speaker: صحير بن عمير
rows.claim: Ṣuḥayr says a perceptive person fulfills what is needed before anyone asks, echoing the verse’s wording about what is asked.
rows.anchor:
صحير بن عمير
29 -
(ثم أفيء بعدها مستقبله ... )
30 -
(ولم أضع ما ينبغي أن أفعله ... )
31 -
(وأفعل العارف قبل المسأله ... )

none: The glossed poems do not explain or illuminate the wording of 14:34.
The love poem and its gloss do not explain or illuminate the wording of 14:34.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The couplet praises a noble, courageous man who has faced death’s dangers and therefore can enter them to dispel a grave crisis.
rows.anchor: لا يكشف الغماء إلا ابن حرة ... يرى غمرات الموت ثم يزروها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn ḥurra signals freedom from tainted ancestry; the label channels Arab concern with mixed lineage into pride and endurance.
rows.anchor: لينبه على زوال الهجنة منه، وخلوص مولده مما يشوبه، وليصير كرمه مهيجا لأنفته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ghamāʾ and related forms share the sense of covering.
rows.anchor: والغماء والغم والغمة والغمم مرجع جميعها إلى التغطية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Then can signal delay between individual words, but not necessarily between clauses; in 90:17 it does not postpone faith until after the listed acts.
rows.anchor: وإن كان في عطفه المفرد على المفرد يدل على التراخي فإنه في عطفه الجملة على الجملة ليس كذاك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qisma stands for muqāsama, and sharr is an accusative verbal noun.
rows.anchor: موضع مقاسمة، أراد شر مقاسمة. وانتصاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ghawāshī means the sword hilts or scabbards, while its ṣudūr are the striking edges; the speaker holds the grips and his enemies take the blades.
rows.anchor: والغواشي: القوائم، وتكون الأغماد أيضا. والصدور، أراد بها المضارب

none: The poem’s phrase from every thing is only a verbal coincidence with 14:34; no gloss connects their meanings.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says responsible transmission requires fulfilling its trust by checking the accuracy of what is reported.
rows.anchor: من تأدية أمانته، وتحري الصحة في روايته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The introduction presents Ibn Jinni as critically testing inherited material, sometimes gently and sometimes forcefully, while pursuing truth fairly and independently.
rows.anchor: لم يكن ابن جني يتقبل كل ما ينقله أو يأخذه على ما خيلت؛ ولكنه كان ينظر فيه وينقده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Jinni defends the reading with a still mīm, arguing Sibawayh accurately transmitted what he heard and that Abu al-ʿAbbās’s alternative cannot fit the poetic meter.
rows.anchor: كما في الاحتجاج لقراءة: "ويعلمهم الكتاب"1 بسكون الميم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar’s tanwīn in taqwā, Ibn Jinni treats the final alif as an augment for morphological matching, and says Sibawayh should have reasoned rather than said he did not know.
rows.anchor: وكما في الاحتجاج لقراءة عيسى بن عمر "على تقوى من الله"1 بالتنوين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Jinni openly transmits the evidence, principles, and debated conclusions he received from his teacher Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī, then adds his own comment.
rows.anchor: ونقل عن شيخه أبي علي الفارسي، فروى مما أنشده إياه من شواهد، وما أخذه عنه من أصول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author sets out to discuss readings outside the seven canonical readers, asking God for aid.
rows.anchor: بادئ بكتاب أذكر فيه أحوال ما شذ عن السبعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He distinguishes plain anomalous readings, which need no discussion, from obscure readings that strain ordinary grammatical analysis and form the book’s focus.
rows.anchor: وضرب ثان وهو هذا الذي نحن على سمته؛ أعني: ما شذ عن السبعة، وغمض عن ظاهر الصنعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For the readings he treats, he combines his own transmissions with accounts verified from others and promises fidelity and accuracy.
rows.anchor: ونحن نورد ذلك على ما رويناه، ثم على ما صح عندنا من طريق رواية غيرنا له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He directs readers to Ibn Mujāhid’s book because it is specifically devoted to anomalous readings and is more trustworthy than many reports from less reliable authorities.
rows.anchor: ننحي4 فيه على كتاب أبي بكر أحمد بن موسى بن مجاهد -رحمه الله- الذي وضعه لذكر الشواذ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abū Ḥātim’s collection is more comprehensive than Qutrub’s because it focuses on readings, while Qutrub gives extensive explanation and supporting evidence.
rows.anchor: غير أن كتاب أبي حاتم أجمع من كتاب قطرب لذلك؛ من حيث كان مقصورا على ذكر القراءات

rows.speaker: محمد بن صالح المصري
rows.claim: Muḥammad ibn Ṣāliḥ reports that Qutrub read from al-Naḥl to the end of the Qurʾān, and that ʿAlī ibn Qutrub read from al-Baqara through al-Naḥl from his father in Egypt in 249 AH.
rows.anchor: قال: حدثني محمد بن صالح المصري2 وراق على بن قطرب، قال: قرأت على أبي محمد بن المستنير قطرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Early qirāʾāt argument was scattered and incomplete, first relying on analogy between similar forms or roots before developing fuller grammatical explanation and citation.
rows.anchor: ثم أخذ يتجه مع ذلك إلى التخريج والاستشهاد

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reads nunshiruha with an open nūn and rāʾ, using 80:22, then إذا شاء أنشره, to support the form against nunshizuhā.
rows.anchor: فابن عباس -المتوفى سنة 68ه- يقرأ: "ننشرها" بالنون المفتوحة والراء1

rows.speaker: عاصم الجحدري
rows.claim: ʿĀṣim al-Jaḥdarī reads malik without an alif and argues that those who read mālik with an alif must also read mālik al-nās in 114:2.
rows.anchor: وعاصم الجحدري -المتوفى سنة 128ه- يقرأ: "ملك يوم الدين" بغير ألف

rows.speaker: عيسى بن عمر
rows.claim: ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar reads al-ṭayr in the accusative in the command to the mountains, construing it as a vocative.
rows.anchor: وعيسى بن عمر -المتوفى سنة 149- يقرأ: {يا جبال أوبي معه والطير} 5 بنصب الطير

rows.speaker: الكسائي
rows.claim: Al-Kisāʾī is reported to read al-dhīb in 12:17 without hamza, while Ḥamza ibn Ḥabīb gives the hamzated form al-dhiʾb.
rows.anchor: ويروون أن الكسائي قرأ أمام حمزة بن حبيب: "فأكله الذيب"6 بغير همز، فقال حمزة

rows.speaker: حمزة بن حبيب
rows.claim: Ḥamza ibn Ḥabīb responds with the hamzated reading of the wolf in contrast to al-Kisāʾī’s unhamzated form.
rows.anchor: بغير همز، فقال حمزة: "الذئب" بالهمزة

rows.speaker: الكسائي
rows.claim: Al-Kisāʾī asks why Hamza marks al-dhiʾb with hamza while leaving al-ḥūt unhamzated, invoking the parallel fish wording; this excerpt ends before Hamza’s answer.
rows.anchor: فقال الكسائي: وكذلك أهمز الحوت "فالتقمه الحؤت"؟ 7 قال: لا
